questions.q: **REMEMBER:** Define literal comprehension and inferential comprehension in your own words. Give one example of each type from the poem "कविता के पन्ने".
questions.a: Literal comprehension: retrieving facts directly stated (e.g., "कविता एक मक्खन है फफूंदी के लिए" — answer: फफूंदी के लिए). Inferential comprehension: deriving implied meaning using evidence (e.g., "कविता बच्चों के लिए खेल क्यों है?" — answer: because children play without fixed rules, just as poetry has no rigid boundaries). A wrong answer that swaps the definitions shows the student cannot distinguish explicit vs. implicit information, leading to misdirected search strategies in exams.

questions.q: **UNDERSTAND:** In the poem "कर", the line "भाषा के पंख नहीं होते" appears. Explain why this is an inferential statement and not a literal fact.
questions.a: The line is metaphorical; language does not literally have wings. The poet implies language can travel, evolve, and reach people without physical movement. A student who says "यह शाब्दिक है क्योंकि कवि ने लिखा है" misses the figurative layer and will fail to answer follow-up inferential questions like "भाषा के पंख न होने का क्या अर्थ है?" because they treat metaphor as fact.

questions.q: **APPLY:** Read the following new stanza (not from NCERT): "सपने वे बीज हैं जो नींद की मिट्टी में उगते हैं / सुबह की धूप में वे फूल बनकर खिलते हैं।" A question asks: "सपने किस मिट्टी में उगते हैं?" Is this literal or inferential? Answer it.
questions.a: Literal. The stanza explicitly states "नींद की मिट्टी में". A student who labels it inferential and writes "सपने मन की मिट्टी में उगते हैं" over-complicates a direct retrieval task, wasting time and risking mark deduction for not quoting the exact phrase.

questions.q: **ANALYZE:** Compare the textbook exercises: Question 1 ("कविता के पन्ने का केंद्रीय भाव लिखिए") and Question 4 ("'फफूंदी' शब्द का प्रयोग कवि ने क्यों किया है?"). Classify each as literal or inferential and justify.
questions.a: Question 1 is inferential — central idea is not stated in one line; it requires synthesizing multiple stanzas. Question 4 is inferential — the word 'फफूंदी' is used literally in the poem, but the *reason* for its use (to show poetry decays rigid minds) must be inferred from context. A student who calls both literal will write plot summaries for Q1 and dictionary meanings for Q4, missing the analytical demand.

questions.q: **EVALUATE:** A student answers the inferential question "कविता को 'खेल' क्यों कहा गया है?" with: "क्योंकि कविता मजेदार होती है।" Critique this answer using the marking scheme expectation of evidence-based reasoning.
questions.a: The answer is insufficient — it states a personal opinion without textual evidence. The marking scheme requires citing lines like "कविता एक खेल है बच्चों के लिए / कविता एक खेल है बड़ों के लिए" and explaining the parallel between play’s freedom and poetry’s lack of fixed rules. A student who gives such vague answers loses 1-2 marks per question in board exams for lack of textual support.

questions.q: **CREATE:** Using the poem "कर", write one literal question and one inferential question that could appear in a board exam. Provide the ideal answer for each.
questions.a: Literal Q: "कविता में 'पतंग' शब्द किसके लिए प्रयुक्त हुआ है?" A: भाषा के लिए (line: "भाषा एक पतंग है"). Inferential Q: "‘डोर’ का टूट जाना भाषा के लिए क्या संकेत करता है?" A: भाषा जब व्याकरण/नियमों की डोर से मुक्त होती है तो वह अनियंत्रित हो सकती है, पर स्वतंत्र भी (evidence: "डोर टूटे तो पतंग उड़ जाए"). A poor created question would be unanswerable from the text (e.g., "कवि का जन्म कब हुआ?") revealing the student doesn’t grasp text-bound comprehension.
